pure-announcement.rationale: This is the vendor's own launch post — 'Today, we're open-sourcing...' with component lists, early-adopter names, a CTO quote and getting-started links — and its one transferable idea, standardizing the model-to-data interface, is stated only at press-release depth with no mechanism.

duplicate.rationale: The corpus's five MCP concepts each treat a specific mechanism (stateless core, extensions, authorization, governance) and presume rather than restate this launch framing, so no single one substantively covers it.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The protocol, SDKs and server repository are all linked and publicly checkable.

durability.rationale: The contents are launch-day snapshot — Claude 3.5 Sonnet, three shipped components, an early-adopter list, promised toolkits — already superseded by MCP's later governance and spec history; only the N-times-M integration problem statement transfers.

actionability.rationale: Its guidance is product onboarding — install desktop servers and follow the quickstart — not a practice or design decision a builder could carry elsewhere.

atomicity.rationale: One subject throughout: the launch of MCP and its pitch.
